answer: Admission is a one-niche mesa watchfire. A registrar issues one numbered rim niche and one forge-stamped ember iron with a filed core assay. Only at published slack may the holder berth at a matching numbered jetty, seat the iron, and hold the niche flame until a shore camera records the stamp against a tide-staff mark. Inspectors match berth log, ember assay, and film. A shared niche, borrowed iron, or off-slack berth collapses to one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive mesa niches, N unique ember irons, and N live slack-water jetty berths that cannot be stacked in one watch.
